questions.question: Build the production cost statement: raw materials opening R60 000, purchases R540 000, carriage R12 000, closing R72 000; factory wages R336 000 plus employer's contributions R24 000; overheads R320 000 plus seventy percent of R40 000 rent; work-in-progress opening R52 000 and closing R40 000; 21 000 units finished. Give every level and the unit cost, and state one valid reading of the unit cost falling from last year's R64.
questions.expected_answer: Direct materials issued: 60 000 plus 540 000 plus 12 000 minus 72 000 — R540 000. Direct labour: 336 000 plus 24 000 — R360 000. Prime cost R900 000. Factory overheads: 320 000 plus 28 000 — R348 000. Total cost of production R1 248 000; add opening work-in-progress 52 000 and subtract closing 40 000 for cost of production of finished goods of R1 260 000. Unit cost: over 21 000 units, R60. Valid readings of the fall: variable cost per unit genuinely dropped through better buying or less waste; or fixed overheads were spread over more units, a volume effect rather than efficiency; or quality was cut, which flatters this year and damages the next — the strong answer separates these before praising management.

questions.question: A shoe factory sells at R240 with variable costs of R150 and fixed costs of R630 000; it produced 8 200 pairs this year against 7 500 pairs and a break-even of 7 600 last year. Calculate the break-even point, this year's profit from the margin, the position in both years, and the effect of leather rising R15 a pair.
questions.expected_answer: Contribution: 240 minus 150 is R90. Break-even: 630 000 over 90 — seven thousand pairs. This year sits 1 200 pairs beyond the line, so profit is 1 200 times 90 — R108 000, fixed costs being already covered. Last year production of 7 500 fell 100 pairs short of the 7 600 break-even, so the factory made a loss of about R9 000 at last year's contribution; the swing to a 1 200-pair safety margin is the improvement worth naming. Dearer leather thins contribution to R75, lifting break-even to 8 400 pairs — above current production — so management must raise the price, renegotiate supply or cut other variable costs, each with its trade-off stated.

questions.question: October's cash from sales given: sales August R180 000, September R200 000, October R220 000; forty percent cash; credit collected fifty percent the next month and forty-five percent the second month with five percent bad. Then settle the VAT: output on R720 000 of exclusive sales, input R79 500, drawings R6 000 excluding VAT, a bad debt of R9 200 inclusive.
questions.expected_answer: October receipts: cash sales forty percent of 220 000 — R88 000; fifty percent of September's credit sales of 120 000 — R60 000; forty-five percent of August's credit sales of 108 000 — R48 600; total R196 600, with the five percent bad debts appearing nowhere because no cash moves. VAT: output fifteen percent of 720 000 — R108 000; minus input 79 500 leaves R28 500; drawings return the input claim, adding fifteen percent of 6 000 — R900; the inclusive bad debt reclaims fifteen over one hundred and fifteen of 9 200 — R1 200 subtracted. Owed to SARS: R28 200, held in trust and never the business's own money.
